sanskrit: jñānavṛddhā mayā rājan bahavaḥ paryupāsitāḥ teṣāṃ kathayatāṃ śaurer ahaṃ guṇavato guṇān samāgatānām aśrauṣaṃ bahūn bahumatān satām
english: O king, I have attended upon many who are great in wisdom. Among those who spoke, I have heard from the assembled sages — those honored by the virtuous — the many and well-esteemed qualities of Śauri (Kṛṣṇa), the man of virtues.

sanskrit: karmāṇy api ca yāny asya janmaprabhṛti dhīmataḥ bahuśaḥ kathyamānāni narair bhūyaḥ śrutāni me
english: And the deeds of this wise one since his very birth, being told repeatedly by men, have been heard by me again and again.

sanskrit: na kevalaṃ vayaṃ kāmāc cedirāja janārdanam na saṃbandhaṃ puraskṛtya kṛtārthaṃ vā kathaṃ cana
english: O king of Cedi, we do not honor Janārdana (Kṛṣṇa) merely out of desire, nor placing kinship first, nor for any personal advantage whatsoever.

sanskrit: arcāmahe 'rcitaṃ sadbhir bhuvi bhaumasukhāvaham yaśaḥ śauryaṃ jayaṃ cāsya vijñāyārcāṃ prayujmahe
english: We worship one who has been worshipped by the good. Understanding his fame, valor, and victory — which bring earthly well-being — we render him honor.

sanskrit: na hi kaś cid ihāsmābhiḥ subālo 'py aparīkṣitaḥ guṇair vṛddhān atikramya harir arcyatamo mataḥ
english: Not one person here, not even a mere boy, has been left unexamined by us. Surpassing all elders in qualities, Hari (Kṛṣṇa) is considered by us the most worthy of worship.

sanskrit: jñānavṛddho dvijātīnāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ balādhikaḥ pūjye tāv iha govinde hetū dvāv api saṃsthitau
english: He is the greatest in wisdom among the twice-born, and superior in strength among the kshatriyas. Both these reasons for worship are established in Govinda (Kṛṣṇa) here.

sanskrit: vedavedāṅgavijñānaṃ balaṃ cāpy amitaṃ tathā nṛṇāṃ hi loke kasyāsti viśiṣṭaṃ keśavād ṛte
english: Knowledge of the Vedas and their auxiliaries, and likewise immeasurable strength — in this world, who among men possesses these distinctions except Keśava (Kṛṣṇa)?

sanskrit: dānaṃ dākṣyaṃ śrutaṃ śauryaṃ hrīḥ kīrtir buddhir uttamā saṃnatiḥ śrīr dhṛtis tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiś ca niyatācyute
english: Generosity, skill, learning, valor, modesty, fame, supreme intelligence, humility, prosperity, steadfastness, contentment, and nourishment — all these are permanently fixed in Acyuta (Kṛṣṇa).

sanskrit: tam imaṃ sarvasaṃpannam ācāryaṃ pitaraṃ gurum arcyam arcitam arcārhaṃ sarve saṃmantum arhatha
english: This one, endowed with all these qualities — teacher, father-figure, and guru; worthy of worship, already worshipped, and deserving of honor — all of you ought to acknowledge him.

sanskrit: ṛtvig gurur vivāhyaś ca snātako nṛpatiḥ priyaḥ sarvam etad dhṛṣīkeśe tasmād abhyarcito 'cyutaḥ
english: Officiating priest, teacher, father-in-law, honored graduate, king, and beloved — all of these roles reside in Hrishikesha (Kṛṣṇa). Therefore Acyuta has been worshipped.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api cāpyayaḥ kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ samarpitam
english: Kṛṣṇa alone is the origin and also the dissolution of the worlds. Indeed, for Kṛṣṇa's sake this entire universe has been offered up.

sanskrit: eṣa prakṛtir avyaktā kartā caiva sanātanaḥ paraś ca sarvabhūtebhyas tasmād vṛddhatamo 'cyutaḥ
english: He is the unmanifest nature, the eternal agent, and beyond all beings. Therefore Acyuta is the most ancient and greatest of all.

sanskrit: buddhir mano mahān vāyus tejo 'mbhaḥ khaṃ mahī ca yā caturvidhaṃ ca yad bhūtaṃ sarvaṃ kṛṣṇe pratiṣṭhitam
english: Intellect, mind, the great principle (mahat), wind, fire, water, ether, and earth — whatever fourfold existence exists — all of it is established in Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: ādityaś candramāś caiva nakṣatrāṇi grahāś ca ye diśaś copadiśaś caiva sarvaṃ kṛṣṇe pratiṣṭhitam
english: The sun, the moon, the constellations, the planets, the directions and sub-directions — all of it is established in Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu puruṣo bālaḥ śiśupālo na budhyate sarvatra sarvadā kṛṣṇaṃ tasmād evaṃ prabhāṣate
english: But this foolish man Śiśupāla does not understand Kṛṣṇa — who is everywhere and at all times — and therefore speaks thus.

sanskrit: yo hi dharmaṃ vicinuyād utkṛṣṭaṃ matimān naraḥ sa vai paśyed yathādharmaṃ na tathā cedirāḍ ayam
english: The wise man who truly examines the highest dharma would see things as they are according to dharma. But this king of Cedi does not see thus.

sanskrit: savṛddhabāleṣv atha vā pārthiveṣu mahātmasu ko nārhaṃ manyate kṛṣṇaṃ ko vāpy enaṃ na pūjayet
english: Among the aged and the young, or among the great-souled kings, who does not consider Kṛṣṇa worthy? And who would not worship him?

sanskrit: athemāṃ duṣkṛtāṃ pūjāṃ śiśupālo vyavasyati duṣkṛtāyāṃ yathānyāyaṃ tathāyaṃ kartum arhati
english: If Śiśupāla resolves that this worship was wrongly performed, then in accordance with justice, he ought to act accordingly in that wrongdoing.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tato bhīṣmo virarāma mahāyaśāḥ vyājahāruttaraṃ tatra sahadevo 'rthavad vacaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the greatly renowned Bhīṣma then fell silent. Thereupon Sahadeva spoke a meaningful reply in that assembly.

sanskrit: keśavaṃ keśihantāram aprameyaparākramam pūjyamānaṃ mayā yo vaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ na sahate nṛpāḥ
english: "Keśava, the slayer of Keśī, who is of immeasurable valor — Kṛṣṇa who is being worshipped by me — whoever among you, O kings, cannot bear this —

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ balināṃ mūrdhni mayedaṃ nihitaṃ padam evam ukte mayā samyag uttaraṃ prabravītu saḥ
english: "— upon the heads of all the mighty ones I have placed this foot. Let him who can properly respond to what I have said now speak his answer."

sanskrit: matimantas tu ye ke cid ācāryaṃ pitaraṃ gurum arcyam arcitam arcārham anujānantu te nṛpāḥ
english: "And those kings here who are wise — let them acknowledge this one who is teacher, father-figure, and guru; worthy of worship, already worshipped, and deserving of honor."

sanskrit: tato na vyājahāraiṣāṃ kaś cid buddhimatāṃ satām mānināṃ balināṃ rājñāṃ madhye saṃdarśite pade
english: Thereupon not one among them spoke — among those wise, virtuous, proud, and powerful kings — with the foot (of supremacy) thus displayed before them.

sanskrit: tato 'patat puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ sahadevasya mūrdhani adṛśyarūpā vācaś cāpy abruvan sādhu sādhv iti
english: Then a rain of flowers fell upon Sahadeva's head, and invisible voices also cried out: "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: āvidhyad ajinaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhaviṣyadbhūtajalpakaḥ sarvasaṃśayanirmoktā nāradaḥ sarvalokavit
english: Nārada, the knower of all worlds, who speaks of past and future, the remover of all doubts, twirled his black deerskin toward Kṛṣṇa (in approval).

sanskrit: tatrāhūtāgatāḥ sarve sunīthapramukhā gaṇāḥ saṃprādṛśyanta saṃkruddhā vivarṇavadanās tathā
english: All those assembled there who had come when summoned — the factions led by Sunitha — appeared enraged and their faces pale with anger.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirābhiṣekaṃ ca vāsudevasya cārhaṇam abruvaṃs tatra rājāno nirvedād ātmaniścayāt
english: The kings there spoke out about the consecration of Yudhiṣṭhira and the honoring of Vāsudeva, with disgust and firm conviction of their own.

sanskrit: suhṛdbhir vāryamāṇānāṃ teṣāṃ hi vapur ābabhau āmiṣād apakṛṣṭānāṃ siṃhānām iva garjatām
english: The appearance of those who were being restrained by their friends shone forth like lions roaring when dragged away from their prey.

sanskrit: taṃ balaugham aparyantaṃ rājasāgaram akṣayam kurvāṇaṃ samayaṃ kṛṣṇo yuddhāya bubudhe tadā
english: Kṛṣṇa then understood that boundless ocean of kings — that inexhaustible ocean of rulers — which was forming a pact (for war), and he perceived the coming battle.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā tu pūjārhaṃ brahmakṣatraṃ viśeṣataḥ sahadevo nṛṇāṃ devaḥ samāpayata karma tat
english: Having honored the one worthy of honor, especially the Brahmin and Kṣatriya orders, Sahadeva — the god among men — completed that rite.

sanskrit: tasminn abhyarcite kṛṣṇe sunīthaḥ śatrukarṣaṇaḥ atitāmrekṣaṇaḥ kopād uvāca manujādhipān
english: When Kṛṣṇa had been thus honored, Sunitha — the crusher of enemies — with eyes reddened with anger, spoke to the assembled lords of men.

sanskrit: sthitaḥ senāpatir vo 'haṃ manyadhvaṃ kiṃ nu sāṃpratam yudhi tiṣṭhāma saṃnahya sametān vṛṣṇipāṇḍavān
english: "I stand here as your commander. What do you think we should do now? Let us arm ourselves and stand in battle against the assembled Vṛṣṇis and Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: iti sarvān samutsāhya rājñas tāṃś cedipuṃgavaḥ yajñopaghātāya tataḥ so 'mantrayata rājabhiḥ
english: Having thus roused all those kings, the chief of the Cedis then consulted with the kings to disrupt the sacrifice.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sāgarasaṃkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpatisāgaram roṣāt pracalitaṃ sarvam idam āha yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, seeing that ocean of kings — resembling the actual ocean — agitated by fury, Yudhiṣṭhira said all this:

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ matimatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vṛddhaṃ kurupitāmaham bṛhaspatiṃ bṛhattejāḥ puruhūta ivārihā
english: He (Yudhiṣṭhira), of great brilliance, like Indra the slayer of enemies, addressed Bhīṣma — the foremost of the wise, the aged grandfather of the Kurus — as Bṛhaspati (the divine teacher):

sanskrit: asau roṣāt pracalito mahān nṛpatisāgaraḥ atra yat pratipattavyaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: "That great ocean of kings has been stirred by fury. Tell me, O grandfather, what should be done here."

sanskrit: yajñasya ca na vighnaḥ syāt prajānāṃ ca śivaṃ bhavet yathā sarvatra tat sarvaṃ brūhi me 'dya pitāmaha
english: "So that there be no obstruction to the sacrifice, and so that well-being comes to the people — tell me everything such that this holds true in all respects, O grandfather."

sanskrit: ity uktavati dharmajñe dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire uvācedaṃ vaco bhīṣmas tataḥ kurupitāmahaḥ
english: When Yudhiṣṭhira, the dharma-knowing king of dharma, had spoken thus, the grandfather of the Kurus, Bhīṣma, then spoke these words:

sanskrit: mā bhais tvaṃ kuruśārdūla śvā siṃhaṃ hantum arhati śivaḥ panthāḥ sunīto 'tra mayā pūrvataraṃ vṛtaḥ
english: "Fear not, O tiger among the Kurus. A dog cannot kill a lion. The auspicious and well-guided path — it was chosen by me here long before."

sanskrit: prasupte hi yathā siṃhe śvānas tatra samāgatāḥ bhaṣeyuḥ sahitāḥ sarve tatheme vasudhādhipāḥ
english: "For just as when a lion is asleep, dogs gathered there would bark at it all together, so too do these lords of the earth."

sanskrit: vṛṣṇisiṃhasya suptasya tatheme pramukhe sthitāḥ bhaṣante tāta saṃkruddhāḥ śvānaḥ siṃhasya saṃnidhau
english: "Standing before the sleeping lion of the Vṛṣṇis — like dogs barking furiously in the presence of a lion — so too do these stand, O dear one."

sanskrit: na hi saṃbudhyate tāvat suptaḥ siṃha ivācyutaḥ tena siṃhīkaroty etān nṛsiṃhaś cedipuṃgavaḥ
english: "For Acyuta, like a sleeping lion, does not yet rouse himself. By this, the man-lion (Narasimha), the chief of Cedis, emboldens them (Śiśupāla's followers) to act like lions."

sanskrit: pārthivān pārthivaśreṣṭha śiśupālo 'lpacetanaḥ sarvān sarvātmanā tāta netukāmo yamakṣayam
english: "O best among kings, the dim-witted Śiśupāla desires, O dear one, to lead all these kings with his whole being to Yama's abode."

sanskrit: nūnam etat samādātuṃ punar icchaty adhokṣajaḥ yad asya śiśupālasthaṃ tejas tiṣṭhati bhārata
english: "Surely Adhokṣaja (Kṛṣṇa) desires to reclaim what is his — the splendor that resides in Śiśupāla — O Bhārata."

sanskrit: viplutā cāsya bhadraṃ te buddhir buddhimatāṃ vara cedirājasya kaunteya sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām
english: "The mind of the king of Cedi — and of all these lords of the earth — has become disordered. May it be well with you, O best of the wise, O son of Kuntī."

sanskrit: ādātuṃ hi naravyāghro yaṃ yam icchaty ayaṃ yadā tasya viplavate buddhir evaṃ cedipater yathā
english: "For whenever this tiger among men (Kṛṣṇa) desires to take from someone, that person's mind becomes disordered — just as has happened with the lord of Cedi."

sanskrit: caturvidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ triṣu lokeṣu mādhavaḥ prabhavaś caiva sarveṣāṃ nidhanaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: "Mādhava (Kṛṣṇa) is the origin and also the destruction of all fourfold beings in the three worlds, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā tataś cedipatir nṛpaḥ bhīṣmaṃ rūkṣākṣarā vācaḥ śrāvayām āsa bhārata
english: Having heard his words, the king, the lord of Cedi, then caused Bhīṣma to hear harsh-syllabled words, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śiśupāla uvāca vibhīṣikābhir bahvībhir bhīṣayan sarvapārthivān na vyapatrapase kasmād vṛddhaḥ san kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: Śiśupāla said: "With your many intimidations, frightening all the kings — why do you not feel shame, old man and disgrace to your lineage?"

sanskrit: yuktam etat tṛtīyāyāṃ prakṛtau vartatā tvayā vaktuṃ dharmād apetārthaṃ tvaṃ hi sarvakurūttamaḥ
english: "It is fitting for you — one who dwells in the third nature (i.e., neither man nor woman) — to speak of matters contrary to dharma, for you are called the foremost among all the Kurus."

sanskrit: nāvi naur iva saṃbaddhā yathāndho vāndham anviyāt tathābhūtā hi kauravyā bhīṣma yeṣāṃ tvam agraṇīḥ
english: "As a boat is bound to a boat, or as one blind man follows another blind man — such indeed are the Kuravas, O Bhīṣma, with you as their leader."

sanskrit: pūtanāghātapūrvāṇi karmāṇy asya viśeṣataḥ tvayā kīrtayatāsmākaṃ bhūyaḥ pracyāvitaṃ manaḥ
english: "By you recounting to us his deeds — beginning with the killing of Putana in particular — our minds have been further unsettled."

sanskrit: avaliptasya mūrkhasya keśavaṃ stotum icchataḥ kathaṃ bhīṣma na te jihvā śatadheyaṃ vidīryate
english: "How, O Bhīṣma, does your tongue not split into a hundred pieces as you, a fool full of arrogance, seek to praise Keśava?"

sanskrit: yatra kutsā prayoktavyā bhīṣma bālatarair naraiḥ tam imaṃ jñānavṛddhaḥ san gopaṃ saṃstotum icchasi
english: "Where younger men would employ censure, O Bhīṣma — this cowherd — you, being senior in wisdom, presume to praise him."

sanskrit: yady anena hatā bālye śakuniś citram atra kim tau vāśvavṛṣabhau bhīṣma yau na yuddhaviśāradau
english: "If in childhood he (Kṛṣṇa) killed Śakuni (the demon) — what is remarkable in that? Or those two — the horse and the bull — O Bhīṣma, who were not skilled in warfare."

sanskrit: cetanārahitaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ yady anena nipātitam pādena śakaṭaṃ bhīṣma tatra kiṃ kṛtam adbhutam
english: "If he knocked down with his foot the cart demon (Shakata) — a piece of wood devoid of consciousness — O Bhīṣma, what wonderful feat was accomplished there?"

sanskrit: valmīkamātraḥ saptāhaṃ yady anena dhṛto 'calaḥ tadā govardhano bhīṣma na tac citraṃ mataṃ mama
english: "If he held aloft a mountain no bigger than an ant-hill for seven days — that Govardhana, O Bhīṣma — I do not consider that remarkable."

sanskrit: bhuktam etena bahv annaṃ krīḍatā nagamūrdhani iti te bhīṣma śṛṇvānāḥ paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ
english: "'Much food was eaten by him while playing on the mountaintop' — those hearing this from you, O Bhīṣma, have been struck with great wonder (at what you say)."

sanskrit: yasya cānena dharmajña bhuktam annaṃ balīyasaḥ sa cānena hataḥ kaṃsa ity etan na mahādbhutam
english: "The powerful Kaṃsa, whose food he ate, O knower of dharma — that same Kaṃsa was killed by him — this too is no great wonder."

sanskrit: na te śrutam idaṃ bhīṣma nūnaṃ kathayatāṃ satām yad vakṣye tvām adharmajña vākyaṃ kurukulādhama
english: "This which I will tell you, O Bhīṣma, O ignorant one, O lowest of the Kuru clan — surely this has not been heard by you from the virtuous who speak."

sanskrit: strīṣu goṣu na śastrāṇi pātayed brāhmaṇeṣu ca yasya cānnāni bhuñjīta yaś ca syāc charaṇāgataḥ
english: "One should not raise weapons against women, cows, and Brahmins; nor against one whose food one has eaten; nor against one who has sought refuge."

sanskrit: iti santo 'nuśāsanti sajjanā dharmiṇaḥ sadā bhīṣma loke hi tat sarvaṃ vitathaṃ tvayi dṛśyate
english: "Thus do the good and virtuous righteous ones always instruct, O Bhīṣma. But in this world, all of that is seen to be false in you."

sanskrit: jñānavṛddhaṃ ca vṛddhaṃ ca bhūyāṃsaṃ keśavaṃ mama ajānata ivākhyāsi saṃstuvan kurusattama goghnaś strīghnaś ca san bhīṣma kathaṃ saṃstavam arhati
english: "You praise Keśava as though not knowing — as one greater in wisdom and age than me — O best of the Kurus. But being a cow-killer and a woman-killer, O Bhīṣma, how does he deserve praise?"

sanskrit: asau matimatāṃ śreṣṭho ya eṣa jagataḥ prabhuḥ saṃbhāvayati yady evaṃ tvadvākyāc ca janārdanaḥ evam etat sarvam iti sarvaṃ tad vitathaṃ dhruvam
english: "If this one who is called lord of the universe, Janārdana, honors himself as the foremost of the wise on account of your words saying 'thus it is' — then surely all of that is false."

sanskrit: na gāthā gāthinaṃ śāsti bahu ced api gāyati prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni bhūliṅgaśakunir yathā
english: "A song does not teach the singer though he may sing much. Beings go to their true nature — as the sparrow and the hawk (each follow their kind)."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ prakṛtir eṣā te jaghanyā nātra saṃśayaḥ ataḥ pāpīyasī caiṣāṃ pāṇḍavānām apīṣyate
english: "Surely this nature of yours is the lowest — there is no doubt in this. And even among the Pāṇḍavas, the nature is considered more wicked than this."

sanskrit: yeṣām arcyatamaḥ kṛṣṇas tvaṃ ca yeṣāṃ pradarśakaḥ dharmavāk tvam adharmajñaḥ satāṃ mārgād avaplutaḥ
english: "You, whose most worthy of worship is Kṛṣṇa, and you who are their guide — you speak the words of dharma, yet you are ignorant of dharma, fallen from the path of the good."

sanskrit: ko hi dharmiṇam ātmānaṃ jānañ jñānavatāṃ varaḥ kuryād yathā tvayā bhīṣma kṛtaṃ dharmam avekṣatā
english: "For who among the best of the wise, knowing himself to be righteous, would act as you have acted, O Bhīṣma, while claiming to regard dharma?"

sanskrit: anyakāmā hi dharmajña kanyakā prājñamāninā ambā nāmeti bhadraṃ te kathaṃ sāpahṛtā tvayā
english: "The maiden named Amba who desired another — how was she abducted by you, O one who fancies himself wise, O knower of dharma? May it be well with you."

sanskrit: yāṃ tvayāpahṛtāṃ bhīṣma kanyāṃ naiṣitavān nṛpaḥ bhrātā vicitravīryas te satāṃ vṛttam anuṣṭhitaḥ
english: "The maiden whom you abducted, O Bhīṣma — your brother Vicitravīrya refused to take her, following the conduct of the virtuous."

sanskrit: dārayor yasya cānyena miṣataḥ prājñamāninaḥ tava jātāny apatyāni sajjanācarite pathi
english: "And the children begotten for another's wives while you, who fancy yourself wise, looked on — born on the path of virtuous conduct (by others for dynastic duty)."

sanskrit: na hi dharmo 'sti te bhīṣma brahmacaryam idaṃ vṛthā yad dhārayasi mohād vā klībatvād vā na saṃśayaḥ
english: "There is no dharma in you, O Bhīṣma. This celibacy you maintain is in vain — out of delusion or impotence, without doubt."

sanskrit: na tv ahaṃ tava dharmajña paśyāmy upacayaṃ kva cit na hi te sevitā vṛddhā ya evaṃ dharmam abruvan
english: "I do not see any benefit in you, O knower of dharma, anywhere. For surely you have not attended upon those elders who have spoken of dharma in this way."

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ dattam adhītaṃ ca yajñāś ca bahudakṣiṇāḥ sarvam etad apatyasya kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm
english: "Sacrifices performed, gifts given, study undertaken, and rituals with great fees — all of this is not worth a sixteenth part of (having) a child."

sanskrit: vratopavāsair bahubhiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati bhīṣma yat sarvaṃ tad anapatyasya moghaṃ bhavati niścayāt
english: "Whatever is accomplished through many vows and fasts, O Bhīṣma — all of that for the childless man is certainly in vain."

sanskrit: so 'napatyaś ca vṛddhaś ca mithyādharmānuśāsanāt haṃsavat tvam apīdānīṃ jñātibhyaḥ prāpnuyā vadham
english: "You, childless and old, because of your false teaching of dharma — like the hamsa (swan/goose), you too may now receive death at the hands of your kinsmen."

sanskrit: evaṃ hi kathayanty anye narā jñānavidaḥ purā bhīṣma yat tad ahaṃ samyag vakṣyāmi tava śṛṇvataḥ
english: "For thus did other men, the knowers of wisdom in former times, speak — O Bhīṣma. That which I will now fully recount to you as you listen:"

sanskrit: vṛddhaḥ kila samudrānte kaś cid dhaṃso 'bhavat purā dharmavāg anyathāvṛttaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ so 'nuśāsti ha
english: "There was once, they say, an old hamsa (goose) living at the ocean's edge in former times — one who spoke of dharma but lived otherwise. He was instructing the birds."

sanskrit: dharmaṃ carata mādharmam iti tasya vacaḥ kila pakṣiṇaḥ śuśruvur bhīṣma satataṃ dharmavādinaḥ
english: "'Practice dharma, not adharma' — so went his words, they say. The birds constantly heard him, O Bhīṣma, speaking of dharma."

sanskrit: athāsya bhakṣyam ājahruḥ samudrajalacāriṇaḥ aṇḍajā bhīṣma tasyānye dharmārtham iti śuśruma
english: "Then for the sake of dharma — so we have heard, O Bhīṣma — the egg-born birds that roam the ocean waters brought food for him (the hamsa)."
